nodes.question: Is the mug positioned to the right of the headphones?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image shows the mug positioned to the right of the headphones; fail if it clearly shows the mug is not to their right; unknown if their relative position cannot be determined. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.
nodes.binding: Compare the mug’s visible position with the headphones in the image. Judge the requested spatial relationship, without requiring a particular editing technique.

nodes.question: Is the mug visibly positioned to the right of the headphones?
nodes.criteria: Apply the original rubric to R1 only. Complete (yes) if the mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones. Absent (no) only if there is clear evidence that no requested change has progressed. Partial if there is evidence of some progress toward moving the mug to the right of the headphones but the requested relationship is not complete. Unknown if required evidence is insufficient or unresolved; do not infer completion, absence, or progress from unrelated edits.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

fulfillment: The edited image shows substantial changes, but the requested relation is not clearly fulfilled: there are multiple mug-like objects, the headphones appear altered/partly obscured, and the original blue mug is not clearly identifiable in its new position. The traces repeatedly assert completion from the same s1/s2 support rather than independently establishing which mug is the target and whether it was moved to the headphones’ right; their near-identical high-confidence wording is not additional evidence. Tighten the binding to the mug in the source image and require the decision to distinguish clear completion from visible but incomplete progress, using the original rubric’s partial outcome when progress is evident but the relation is not complete, and unknown when target identity or position cannot be resolved. Do not infer absence from ambiguity or treat unrelated object changes as progress. The reference label is an aggregate constraint, not atomic ground truth; investigate the mismatch against the actual images and criterion. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated here.
s2: The binding is too generic: the source clearly identifies one blue mug left of the headphones, while the edited image contains multiple mug-like objects and the blue mug is only a blurred shape. Anchor the comparison to the source mug’s identity and assess its edited position relative to the headphones; do not let any mug on the right satisfy the check by object category alone. Require evidence to state which object is being tracked and what is visibly established about its position. Preserve the rubric’s distinction: pass only when the target mug’s requested relation is clear, partial when its movement toward that relation is evident but incomplete, and unknown when identity or position cannot be resolved; do not turn ambiguity into either completion or absence. The repeated high-confidence pass traces reuse the same unsupported identification and are not independent corroboration, so calibrate confidence to the visual evidence. Treat the partial reference as an aggregate diagnostic, not atomic ground truth. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
s1: The binding currently checks only whether some mug and headphones are visible, so it can pass despite failing to establish the requested edit. Make this support node track the specific source mug (the blue mug, initially left of the headphones) across the images, and report whether its identity and position relative to the headphones are actually discernible in the edited image. The edit contains multiple mug-like objects and a blurred blue shape, so category-level matching and confident claims that the relation is observable are not enough; require evidence to distinguish the tracked mug from added objects and state what is clear versus ambiguous. Keep this node focused on evidence availability rather than deciding fulfillment: ambiguity should remain unresolved, not be treated as absence or completion. The repeated near-identical high-confidence passes are not independent evidence; calibrate confidence to the visual support. Use the partial reference only as an aggregate diagnostic alongside the rubric and images. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
